The Discourse on "Perhaps":
Does the past exist?
Perhaps it exists, perhaps it does not.
"It exists, yet it does not exist"?
One should not say that... [as before] ...
"It exists, yet it does not exist"? One should not say that.
“Yes,” [you say].

“Then is ‘existent’ (atthaṭṭha) ‘non-existent’ (natthaṭṭha), and ‘non-existent’ ‘existent’; is existence non-existence, and non-existence existence; or are ‘it exists’ and ‘it does not exist,’ or ‘it does not exist’ and ‘it exists,’ identical, one in meaning, equal, equivalent, and of the same nature?
You should not speak thus… [and so on].
Is it that the future exists?
It is both that it exists and that it does not exist. Is it that it both exists and does not exist? It is both that it exists and that it does not exist.
It should not be said thus ...
[as before] ... Is it that there is service, but no one who serves? Yes.

Is "existent-meaning" the same as "non-existent-meaning," and "non-existent-meaning" the same as "existent-meaning"? Is "existence" the same as "non-existence," and "non-existence" the same as "existence"? Are "it exists" and "it does not exist," or "it does not exist" and "it exists," identical, one in meaning, equal, of the same nature, and of the same kind?
You should not say so... [and so on].
Does the present exist?
"If it is not so, then is it that 'it is so' and 'it is not so'? One should not say this... [and so on]."
“Is there ‘it is’ and ‘it is not’?”— “Yes. “Then is the meaning of ‘it is’ the meaning of ‘it is not’?”— [and so on].
Is it the case that [the action] is of the same kind as that which belongs to the same homogeneous class?
One should not say so… [etc.
…Does the past exist, or does it not exist?
“Yes, [it exists]. “In what way does it exist, and in what way does it not exist?
“The past exists as ‘past’; the past does not exist as ‘future,’ nor does the past exist as ‘present.’”
"It exists, yet it does not exist"?
One should not say that... [as before] ...
"It exists, yet it does not exist"? One should not say that.
“Yes,” you say.

“Is ‘existent’ the meaning of ‘non-existent,’ and ‘non-existent’ the meaning of ‘existent’? Is ‘existence’ the meaning of ‘non-existence,’ and ‘non-existence’ the meaning of ‘existence’? Are ‘it exists’ and ‘it does not exist,’ or ‘it does not exist’ and ‘it exists,’ identical, one in meaning, equal, equivalent, and of the same nature?
You must certainly not say so… [and so on].
"Is it the case that the future both exists and does not exist?
"Yes.
"In what way does it exist, and in what way does it not exist?"
"That the future is future—this indeed exists; that the future is past—this indeed does not exist; that the future is present—this indeed does not exist.
"Is it the case that this exists and this does not exist?
One should not say so... [and so forth].
"Is it that 'it exists' means 'it does not exist,' and 'it does not exist' means 'it exists'? "Yes.
"Does the meaning of 'it exists' mean 'it does not exist,' and the meaning of 'it does not exist' mean 'it exists'? ... [and so on] ...
"Is it the case that [a feeling] born from that [contact] is of the same kind and has the same quality?
"One should not say so... pe ...
Is it the case that the present [feeling] both exists and does not exist?"
“Yes,” [he said].
“In what sense does it exist, and in what sense does it not exist?
“In this sense it exists: the present exists as ‘present. In this sense it does not exist: the present does not exist as ‘past,’ nor does the present exist as ‘future.’”
"It is well-being, it is not well-being"?
One should not say that... [as before] ... "It is well-being, it is not well-being"? One should not say that.
“Yes. “Does it have the sense of ‘is’ and the sense of ‘is not,’ ... [and so on] ...
being the same, having an equal portion, and being of that same kind?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … It should not be said:
“The past both exists and does not exist.”
“Is the future both existent and non-existent?
Is the present both existent and non-existent?”—
“Yes.”
Is it the case that the past is the future? Is it the case that the past is the present? Is it the case that the future is the past?
Is it the case that the future is the present? Is it the case that the present is the past? Is it the case that the present is the future? One should not say so.
… [as before] … Therefore, the past either exists or does not exist; the future either exists or does not exist; the present either exists or does not exist.
Does form exist?
"If it is not so, then is it that 'it is' and yet 'it is not'?
One should not say this... [and so on]."
“Is it that ‘it exists’ is the same as ‘it does not exist’?”—“Yes.

“Then is the meaning of existence the meaning of non-existence, and the meaning of non-existence the meaning of existence? Is being existent being non-existent, and being non-existent being existent? Are ‘it exists’ and ‘it does not exist,’ or ‘it does not exist’ and ‘it exists,’ identical, one in meaning, the same, equal, and of the same nature?”
It should not be said thus … [and so on] … feeling … perception …
“Are volitional formations … consciousness existent? “Yes, they are existent;
yes, they are non-existent.”
"It is well-being, it is not non-existence"?
One should not say that... [as before] ...
"It is well-being, it is not non-existence"? One should not say that.
“Yes.
“Is it of the same meaning, of a non-existent meaning … [and so on] … of the same kind and of equal status?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that material form both exists and does not exist? Yes.
What exists, and what does not exist?
Form indeed exists as "form," but form does not exist as "feeling" ... [and so on] ...
form does not exist as "perception" ... [and so on].
"Form is formations"—this indeed does not exist...
"Form is consciousness"—this indeed does not exist.
Is it that "it exists" and yet "it does not exist"?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it that there is service, or is there no service? Yes.
Is it the case that "having the meaning of 'is'" and "having the meaning of 'is not'" ... [and so on] ... are the same, equal, and of the same kind?
One should not say so ... [and so on] ... .
Feeling … perception … volitional formations …
"Is consciousness indeed existent, or is it indeed non-existent?
"Yes.
"In what way is it existent, and in what way is it non-existent?"
Consciousness exists as consciousness alone;
consciousness does not exist as form …pe… consciousness does not exist as feeling …pe…
"Consciousness is perception"—this indeed does not exist...
"consciousness is mental formations"—this indeed does not exist.
Is it that "it exists" and "it does not exist"?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it that there is service, but no one who serves? Yes.
“Is it the case that ‘the meaning of eight’ is not the meaning of non-existence … [and so on] … that they are the same, equal, and of the same kind?
“One must certainly not say so … [and so on] …”
It should not be said:
"Form exists, or it does not exist"; [the same applies to] feeling...
Is perception ...
formations ...
consciousness thus existent, or thus non-existent?
“Yes.

“Perception … volitional formations … consciousness is form,” so it is said. …
Is it the case that consciousness is feeling?
Is it the case that consciousness is perception?
Is it the case that consciousness is mental formations?
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Therefore, matter both exists and does not exist;
feeling … [and so on].
"Perception...
volitional formations...
consciousness: does it exist, or does it not exist?"
The Discussion on Rainy Weather is finished.
Its summary verse is:
Availability, decline, ...
The dwelling in the holy life is specific;
full understanding is the abandoning of sensual lust;
the doctrine of "all exists" is the sense-sphere.
The past and the future are divisions of beauty;
all phenomena are foundations of mindfulness.
"It is indeed so," "it is not so."
The Great Chapter.
